newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-LEIGHTON SEES OP. PROFIT MAINTAINED.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-LEIGHTON SEES OP. PROFIT MAINTAINED.

text.p: Construction group Leighton Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it expected operating revenue and operating profit to be maintained in the current year to June 30, 1998.

"The overall outlook continues to be positive," Leighton chief executive Wal King said in a statement accompanying its 1996/97 results. "The directors expect operating revenue and operating profit to be maintained next year," King said.

Leighton reported a pre-abnnormals net profit for the year to June 30, 1997 of A$86.24 million, up 32 percent from the previous year and above the range of A$79 million to A$85.4 million forecast by analysts.
Net profit after abnormals was A$132.11 million, up from A$70.21 million a year earlier because of an after-tax abnormal gain of A$46 million.
This abnormal gain came from from the sale of subsidiary Welded Mesh for A$140 million and the sale of investments in Ipco International and the Australia's Wonderland theme park.
Leighton announced a final dividend of 13 cents, up from 8.5 cents the previous year. It also announced a special dividend of 10 cents per share because of the substantial abnormal gain.

Leighton said its operating revenue rose 22 percent to A$2.93 billion, with civil engineering contributing A$957 million, non-residential building A$926 million and contract mining A$719 million. It said uncompleted work at hand stood at a record A$4.23 billion to the year 2002.

Leighton's total cash at the end of June 30 rose to A$422.84 million from A$165.84 million a year earlier. "The group's balance sheet is in a very healthy psosition with no net debt and total assets of A$1.62 billion," the company said.
"A strong financial base provides a solid platform for long term growth," King said.
Leighton's annual earnings per share rose to 50.9 cents per share from 29.1 cents a year earlier.
King said operations in both Australia and Asia exceeded expectations.
"Whilst the Australian economy remains somewhat flat, the non-residential construction industry appears certain to continue its upward cycle, particularly in engineering construction," King said.
Transport infrastructure such as roadworks would be a key driver of civil engineering activity, he said.
There would also be public and private sector opportunities in rail, airports and port developments, he said.
"The newly deregulated telecommunications environment should create some interesting business developments, as should electricity and oil and gas projects," he said.
Mining prospects and related infrastructure works also looked positive. The commercial building market was improving in Australia, King said.
Property activities for the group would remain focused in Sydney with a new development in North Sydney expected to start construction in the next six months, he said.
Confidence in Hong Kong remained high and Leighton's forward order book in Indonesia had doubled over the past 12 months.
"Prospects continue to be promising," King said of the group's Indonesian operations. Leighton's shares were up 37 cents at A$6.15 at 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT).
